beats.words: Disney asked a dying AI firm to go bust first. That way it could hire the team and leave the lawsuits behind.
beats.point: The hook: a buyer told a company to go bankrupt first, and why that is strange

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.motion: still; the label types in on "go bust"

beats.words: So why are Disney and Google both paying for pieces of the same company? And what does it mean for you?
beats.point: Two very different giants paid for the same company, so there must be two reasons

picture.what: Google and Disney wordmarks either side of the Character.AI logo, equal size, on the ink desk

beats.motion: the two logos slide in on their names

beats.words: I've been reading the court papers on Character.AI, the app where millions of people chat with made-up characters.
beats.point: This comes from the bankruptcy paperwork, not gossip

picture.what: Character.AI's Chapter 11 announcement, the line about the voluntary Chapter 11 filing highlighted

beats.motion: slow push into the highlighted line

beats.words: Two giants have now paid for pieces of it, for very different reasons. So I wanted to break it down for you.
beats.point: He is going to unpack two different reasons, one at a time

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Let's start with Google. Google wanted the brains behind the app.
beats.point: Google is first, and it wanted the people

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: So in 2024, it reportedly paid two point seven billion dollars to use Character.AI's tech. And it hired the founders and their research team away.
beats.point: What Google got for its money: the tech and the founders, printed as the first receipt

picture.what: Receipt 1 prints line by line on cream paper: GOOGLE · AUG 2024 / Use of the tech ... $2.7B (reported) / Hires: the founders + research team

beats.motion: each line prints on the word that names it

beats.words: Google was racing to build the smartest AI, and these people were very good at it.
beats.point: Why Google wanted them: the race to build the smartest AI

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: But the rest of the staff stayed behind, and the app carried on, until its cash started running low.
beats.point: Most of the company stayed behind after Google took the founders

picture.what: Wired's report, the words "vast majority" of staff stayed highlighted

beats.motion: push in to the highlighted words

beats.words: Now, Disney wanted something else, and to see why, go back to last December.
beats.point: Disney had a different reason, and it starts a year earlier

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Disney agreed to put a billion dollars into OpenAI. As part of that deal, over two hundred Disney characters would star in Sora, OpenAI's video app.
beats.point: Disney first tried to put its characters inside someone else's AI app

picture.what: The December 2025 Disney and OpenAI announcement: $1 billion and 200+ characters for Sora, highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps the $1 billion line, then the 200 characters line

beats.words: But Sora belonged to OpenAI. So Disney was really renting space for Mickey, Marvel and Star Wars on someone else's app.
beats.point: Owning the characters is different from owning the app they live in: Disney was renting

picture.what: Marvel, Star Wars and Disney wordmarks sit inside an outlined box labelled SORA, with OpenAI's logo on the box's door

beats.motion: the box outline draws round them on "someone else's app"

beats.words: Then in March, OpenAI shut Sora down.
beats.point: The landlord closed the building

picture.what: OpenAI's 24 March 2026 announcement that Sora is shutting down, dated

beats.motion: cut on "shut"

beats.words: The deal died, and no money changed hands.
beats.point: The deal ended with nothing paid

picture.what: A receipt for the Disney and OpenAI deal stamped VOID; total line reads $0 changed hands

beats.motion: the VOID stamp lands on "died"

beats.words: Disney said it respected the decision, which is a very polite way to say, well, that's awkward.
beats.point: The joke lands on his face: Disney being polite about it

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.motion: hold still on "that's awkward"

beats.words: So Disney changed its plan. In September, it hired Character.AI's chief executive, who ran the firm after the founders left. He got a brand new job, Disney's first ever technology chief.
beats.point: Disney's new plan starts with hiring the person who ran Character.AI

picture.what: The report that Disney hired Character.AI's chief executive as its first chief technology officer, highlighted

beats.motion: push in on "first chief technology officer"

beats.words: And this month, the court papers show the rest of the plan. Disney has offered jobs to sixty-six of Character.AI's staff. All together, their pay comes to about sixty million dollars a year, for three years.
beats.point: What Disney is paying for the people, printed as the second receipt

picture.what: Receipt 2 starts printing: DISNEY · OCT 2026 / 66 staff ... about $60M a year x 3 years

beats.motion: the line prints on "sixty-six"

beats.words: On top of that, Disney has bid twenty million dollars for the code. That includes its tools for keeping children safe.
beats.point: And what Disney is paying for the code, including its child-safety tools

picture.what: Receipt 2 adds: The code (opening bid) ... $20M, with sub-lines trust and safety tools, age prediction

beats.motion: the line prints on "twenty million"

beats.words: Here's the clever bit.
beats.point: He flags the trick before he explains it

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Character.AI filed for bankruptcy on the twelfth of October.
beats.point: The bankruptcy is real and dated

picture.what: The Chapter 11 announcement again, the date line highlighted

beats.motion: cut on "bankruptcy"

beats.words: And Disney made that a condition of its offer, and the papers even say why. Character.AI was running low on cash. And it faced lawsuits from families and US states, who say its chatbots harmed children.
beats.point: The filing itself says why Disney wanted the court: cash running out and lawsuits

picture.what: The court filing itself: "diminishing cash reserve and significant litigation and regulatory risks", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps the quoted words as he says "cash", then "lawsuits"

beats.words: Going through the court means Disney takes the people and the code, clean, while the lawsuits stay behind with Character.AI.
beats.point: The money map: the people and the code go to Disney, the lawsuits stay in the old company

picture.what: The money map: an arrow carries THE PEOPLE and THE CODE from the Character.AI box to Disney; THE LAWSUITS stays inside the box

beats.motion: the two labels slide out on "takes"; the lawsuits label stays put

beats.words: So who is left holding the empty box?
beats.point: The question the rest of the story answers: who gets nothing

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: The people who used the app, for a start. Disney didn't bid for the app itself, or for anyone's chats. So what happens to the app is now up to the court.
beats.point: The users are left out: Disney did not bid for the app or anyone's chats

picture.what: The empty box, ink outline: THE APP and USERS' CHATS drop in; a label NOT IN DISNEY'S BID (the filing excludes consumer-facing apps and end user data)

beats.motion: each label drops in on its words

beats.words: And then there are the people suing Character.AI, whose claims stay with a firm that is being sold for parts.
beats.point: The people suing are left with a company being sold for parts

picture.what: The empty box gains THE LAWSUITS: families and US states

beats.motion: the label drops in on "suing"

beats.words: See, the money followed the people. Google paid billions for the tech and the founders, and Disney is paying millions for the rest of the team. Everyone else is left with the empty box.
beats.point: The whole story in one picture: two receipts and an empty box

picture.what: The one picture: Receipt 1 (Google, 2024, $2.7B, the founders) and Receipt 2 (Disney, 2026, $20M code + $60M a year team) side by side, the empty box beside them with nothing going in

beats.motion: the camera pulls back to show all three; hold

beats.words: And it isn't just Disney. Netflix bought an AI film start-up this year, and the record label Warner Music bought an AI firm too.
beats.point: Disney is part of a pattern: other media giants have bought AI firms this year

picture.what: Netflix logo with InterPositive ($587M, reported) and Warner Music Group logo with Sureel AI (June), each with its source line

beats.motion: each pair arrives on its name

beats.words: The big media firms have stopped renting AI, and started owning it.
beats.point: The shift in one line: renting AI to owning it

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: So my prediction is that three more giants follow them. First, Skydance, the new owner of Paramount Pictures. Then the record label Universal Music. And then Comcast, the American TV giant that owns NBC.
beats.point: The prediction names three companies that have not bought yet

picture.what: Three empty receipt slots, each with a logo: Skydance (Paramount), Universal Music Group, Comcast (NBCUniversal)

beats.motion: each logo lands on its name

beats.words: By the first of March, 2027, I reckon each of them will announce buying an AI firm or its team. And I'm seventy-five percent sure all three will do it.
beats.point: The call is checkable: a date and a confidence

picture.what: Prediction card: BY 1 MARCH 2027, the three logos, 75%

beats.motion: the 75% counts up on "seventy-five"

beats.words: Now, why should you care if you're not Disney? Because most businesses now run on someone else's AI.
beats.point: Why it matters to a business that is not Disney

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: It might be your writing tool, your chatbot, or maybe your whole customer service desk. If that supplier goes the way of Sora, the tool can switch off. And your work in it can go too.
beats.point: It already happened once in this story: an AI app switched off and took the deal with it

picture.what: The Sora shutdown page again, dated

beats.motion: cut on "switch off"

beats.words: And this story shows the warning signs, years before the end. Here's what I'd do with this info if I were you. Pick the AI tool your business leans on most, and ask four things about the firm that makes it.
beats.point: He moves to what he would do, and the warning signs come first

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: First, are its founders still there? Google took Character.AI's founders two years before the end.
beats.point: Warning sign one, with this story's proof: the founders left two years early

picture.what: Checklist card 1 of 4: FOUNDERS STILL THERE? with the dates AUG 2024 and OCT 2026

beats.motion: the card ticks in

beats.words: Second, is your tool the main thing that firm sells, or a side bet? Sora was a side bet, and it vanished.
beats.point: Warning sign two: Sora was a side bet and vanished

picture.what: Checklist card 2 of 4: MAIN PRODUCT OR SIDE BET? with Sora, shut 24 Mar 2026

beats.words: Third, is the firm running short of cash? The court papers warned about exactly that.
beats.point: Warning sign three: the filing warned about cash

picture.what: Checklist card 3 of 4: SHORT OF CASH? with "diminishing cash reserve" quoted

beats.words: And fourth, is it collecting lawsuits? That's why Disney went through the court.
beats.point: Warning sign four: the lawsuits are why Disney used the court

picture.what: Checklist card 4 of 4: COLLECTING LAWSUITS?

beats.words: If two of those answers worry you, line up a plan B now. That means a second tool you've tried on real work, and a copy of your own data.
beats.point: The action: two worrying answers means a tested second tool and a copy of your data

picture.what: Krish to camera, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: The full deep dive is at makeyourmindup.ai.
beats.point: Where to read the whole piece

picture.what: End card: makeyourmindup.ai on the brand ink, follow.the.money series mark

beats.motion: hold
